The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${h}^{′}(3)$ where $h(x)=f(x)+g(x).$
after.worked_solution:
The addition rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)+{g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(3)={f}^{′}(3)+{g}^{′}(3).
$$

Also, notice that $x=3$ corresponds to

- the interval $x\in (2,4)$ for the function $f,$ and

- the interval $x\in (2.5,4)$ for the function $g,$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039683/assets/19a32fa6a7b2b6481052ab3539838bb00d486f92ea3f08b54efa2a1cfc69d221.png)

- The slope of $y=f(x)$ is constant on $x\in (2,4)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{0-2}{4-2}=-1.
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(3)=-1.$

- The slope of $y=g(x)$ is constant on $x\in (2.5,4)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δg}{Δx}=\frac{1-1}{4-2.5}=0.
$$

Therefore, ${g}^{′}(3)=0.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(3) & ={f}^{′}(3)+{g}^{′}(3) \\  & =-1+0 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
